modes.name: Chain Campaign
steps: Clear Normal, Elite and Boss levels on each Depth map, then claim the level rewards to open the next Depth.
Kill the Elite directly to chain-clear every Normal level after it; kill the Boss directly to chain-clear the whole Depth.
Kill all enemies within the turn limit to trigger a Chain and clear related levels at once; tap the map chest to claim them.
After Auto-Battle unlocks, spend Chain Licenses (1 per battle; they reset to 10 daily at 05:00).
Tap the Idle Farming chest before it hits its cap.
Open Fragment Chests as they finish; higher Depth gives better chests (UR chests start above Depth 60).
modes.tip: Don't spend Diamonds to skip chest timers.
modes.why: Its Depth unlocks other modes (Assignments, World Boss at Depth 15, Unlimited Recruitment milestones) and raises idle-farm income.

modes.name: Exploration (story maps)
steps: Walk the map, fight enemies and open Treasure Caskets for points.
Watch HP: characters in an Exploration team don't recover lost HP after battles.
Finish the main goal quests to finalize the map and get its rewards.
At 20% Exploration Progress, use Sweep Coupons to collect all Map Rewards instantly.
modes.team: Team 1; swap a fresh unit in if HP runs low.
modes.tip: Free Stages have 3-star goals; star totals pay Diamonds. Reverse Mode replays the story from the enemy side with its own 3-star goals.

modes.name: Conquest Battle (bosses) and Formidable
steps: Read the boss's characteristics, then set a team that answers them.
Strike the boss's weak points during the fight for extra rewards.
Invite other players to fight together if you can't solo it.
Only spend attempts you can win: Conquest Coupons are deducted only on victory, and a failed start costs just 1 Stamina.
For Formidable bosses (no Stamina cost), clear them in order; server-wide clear counts unlock bonus rewards.
modes.team: Team 1. Bring Yakumo [Jason] against bosses that heal.
modes.tip: Farm the boss of the Modification path you chose for Nutcracker's cells (then Rize's).
modes.unlock: Story progress; Formidable after clearing [Yamori] Conquest - Abyss
modes.why: Drops Modification materials for UR cells (each Modification path has its own boss).

modes.name: Force Challenge (Biography)
steps: Pick your team first: it's locked for the whole run.
Fight 3 stages in a row; HP carries over between them.
Expect enemies to gain random passive skills.
Clear as many stages as you can: more stages mean better Finalization Rewards.
Don't fear failing: a loss costs only 1 Stamina.
modes.team: Team 1. Naki's back-up healing (8% max HP each turn to allies hit last turn) helps HP last across 3 stages.
modes.tip: Half-cost Stamina on new servers (days 1-28) covers Biography.

modes.name: Blockade Breakthrough
steps: Pick the day's buff effects; they can't be changed after you confirm.
Clear stages in order; every owned character can take part.
Rotate units: lost HP is not restored, and no healing goes above a unit's pre-fight HP.
Respawns (revive one unit to 100%) only come with a Monthly Login Contract.
Come back daily: it resets every day. Spend tokens in the Blockade Breakthrough Shop.
Use your VIP manual reset attempts (VIP levels unlock them) to replay stages for a second round of rewards.
modes.team: Use all 3 teams' units so fresh HP is always available.
modes.tip: Sweep unlocks at a set Chain Campaign Depth.

modes.name: Assignments (Bounty and Urgent)
steps: Dispatch eligible characters to Bounty Assignments and wait out the timer.
Fight the battle-type Bounty and Boss Assignments directly.
Meet the bonus goals for extra rewards; they don't block completion.
After 5-7 Bounty Assignments, an Urgent Assignment (co-op boss) may trigger; the first successful run pays Conquest Rewards.
Ask friends or strangers to help on Urgent Assignments after your first try.
Around the 9th-16th Bounty, an Assignment Sale can appear : buy only the Gold-priced items and skip the Diamond-priced ones.
modes.team: Any eligible characters for dispatch; team 1 for battles.
modes.tip: Urgent Assignment tier rises with Depth (A at 20-35, S at 36-50).

modes.name: Abyssal Battlefield (weekly rogue-like)
steps: Choose 1 character to bring in. Units below full stars are treated as full stars, so bring your best kit, not your highest star.
Move 1 grid at a time; you can't go back after a grid's event.
After each normal-map win, pick 1 buff (re-roll with simulation coins).
Beat each normal map's final boss to advance; after 3 normal maps, 3 hard maps open (no buffs there).
Don't quit mid-battle: losing or exiting fails the run.
Collect Abyss Coins from moves, battles, bosses and chests.
modes.team: Nutcracker or Sen: units are treated as full stars here, so you see their 1-star and 3-star passives working.
modes.tip: Collect Abyss Coins every week; the run fails if you lose or quit mid-battle.
modes.unlock: Weekly event; Chain Level 130 and server day 40+

modes.name: Region Breakthrough (Carnival)
modes.region: game text of September 22, 2026; confirm on your server

items: Pick a stage. Save a line-up: those characters are locked in until the stage is cleared or all of them are dead.
The region map shows enemy groups: Boss, Elite and Normal. Tap a group for its CP, drops and Extermination share.
Select one or more groups for one fight; each selected group raises the total CP. They enter in the order you picked, and from the 5th on they wait in back-up and step in when a slot frees.
Win to collect every selected group's Extermination progress. HP and progress are kept after every fight.
Defeat every boss and reach 100% Extermination to clear the stage. If your whole team dies, the attempt fails; Give Up resets the area.
sections.title: How a stage works

items: Read the modifiers first: Fixed Modifiers (2 effects that swap each week) and Regional Modifiers (more as the stage number rises) add passives to listed enemy types.
Check each group's CP before you add it: every group you add raises the fight's total CP.
Fight bosses while your team still has most of its HP, because lost HP never comes back inside the stage.
Your first clear is rated by how many battles you entered; a better rating pays a better first-clear reward. Fewer battles probably rate better. (unconfirmed)
sections.title: Planning a stage

items: Healing and shields matter more here than anywhere else, because HP carries over. (worked out from the rules — not tested)
Area damage: every group you select enters the same fight. (worked out from the rules — not tested)
Bring your best 5: enemy groups beyond the 4th step in from back-up, so long fights need staying power. (worked out from the rules — not tested)
sections.title: What to build

items: Weekly settlement: Monday 05:00 (server time). The weekly reward follows the highest stage you cleared that week, and needs at least 1 clear.
After settlement your progress resets and your starting cap is set by last week: more than 7 stages → 9, 6–7 → 7, 3–5 → 4, 0–2 → 2.
When the Carnival ends, your highest stage pays the Carnival reward and sets where you start next Carnival.
Stages and sweeps pay Carnival Tokens (1–13 per stage in the first Carnival's table, game data quoted in the research notes), and you get 3 free sweeps a day.
sections.title: Weekly cycle and rewards

Creator video: Aslan beginner guide (6Lcdb56rRng, October 25, 2026)
steps: Stages unlock in order. The higher the stage, the harder it is and the better the rewards.
Save a line-up to enter: those characters are locked in, and lost HP carries over from fight to fight until the stage is cleared or the whole team is dead.
On the map, tap enemy groups to add them to one fight. Each group adds CP; enemies after the 4th wait in back-up and step in.
Defeat every boss and reach 100% Extermination to clear the stage.
If your whole team dies, the run fails. Give Up resets the area.
Your first clear is rated by how many battles you entered, and a better rating pays a better first-clear reward.
Every enemy gets Fixed Modifiers (they swap each week) and Regional Modifiers (by stage number).

Weekly reset: Monday 05:00 (server time). Clear at least 1 stage that week for the weekly reward. Next week you can start up to stage 9 if you cleared more than 7, stage 7 for 6–7, stage 4 for 3–5, stage 2 for 0–2.
When the Carnival ends, your highest stage pays the Carnival reward and sets where you start next Carnival.
modes.teams_needed: 1 saved line-up per run; it stays locked until the stage ends.
modes.tip: Enemies gain Fixed Modifiers (rotate weekly) and Regional Modifiers by stage number.
tips: Common mistake: entering a stage with an injured team.
Common mistake: a week with no clear: no weekly reward, and your cap drops to stage 2.
Common mistake: Give Up by accident; it resets the area's progress.
Use the 3 free sweeps every day.
Sweeps pay Carnival Tokens; keep spare Tokens for later Carnivals. (creator tip)
modes.why: The Carnival's stage mode: clear stages in order, each harder with better rewards. Stages and daily sweeps pay Carnival Tokens.

modes.name: Tower Trials
steps: Pick the right trial: STR/SKL/SPD trials only take that type (PSY, WIT and DST go anywhere); faction trials only take that faction.
Clear main stages in order; some unlock EX stages.
Check each stage's special rules before fighting.
On hard Elite stages, open other players' clear teams in the stage details and copy them.
modes.team: No Organization trial: Rize, Nutcracker, Sen and Kurona on the field, Shu in back-up. PSY, WIT and DST units fill any attribute trial, but none of your free units is one: field STR units in STR trials (Nutcracker, Shu [Gourmet], Yakumo [Jason], Kureo, Enji), SPD units in SPD trials (Kurona, Sen) and SKL units in SKL trials (Rize, Naki).
modes.tip: Each stage pays once; there's no reason to retry a cleared stage.

modes.name: Stronghold Annihilation
modes.region: game text of September 22, 2026; confirm on your server

items: Only the top 3 Organizations from that Saturday's Stronghold Takeover enter.
Preparation 15:30: set line-ups and view the map. Battle 16:00–17:00 (server time).
sections.title: Phases and timeline

items: Strongholds have several levels, each with a different number of defenders, CP and rewards.
Each stronghold has a required CP: a team below it can't attack that stronghold.
When all defenders of a stronghold are beaten, it is settled and pays out by each Organization's ranking in that stronghold.

Scale on an older server (April 2026): Aslan's screen showed strongholds needing about 0.9M, 1.2M and 1.5M CP, Lv.3 NPC defenders at 1.1M CP and over 6,000 defenders left. Your server's numbers will differ. (from video, Aslan, 5:00)
sections.title: The map and CP minimums

items: 1 team per battle. HP lost stays lost and comes back slowly outside battle.
Fallen characters come back after a wait (1,200 s in the game settings), or revive at once with Diamonds or Quick Recovery Potions; each revive in a row costs more, and both pay Revival Points.
Kiyoko's +40% works in Stronghold Takeover only; her passive does not mention Annihilation, so don't count on it here.
sections.title: Teams, HP and revives

items: Send each team at the highest stronghold its CP allows.
Settle one stronghold at a time with the whole Organization, so it pays out while you still rank high in it. (worked out from the rules — not tested)
sections.title: Choosing targets

items: Organizations are ranked by their members' total Annihilation Points; personal rewards follow your own Annihilation Points and Activity Points.
Rank rewards include Potential Lucky Coins (5–6 at rank 1) and 50 Limit Crystals. (game data quoted in the research notes)
sections.title: Rewards

items: Before 16:00, agree which stronghold the Organization settles first, and send every team that passes its CP minimum there.
One strong team can beat many defenders in a row (the frame on this page shows players with 13, 52 and 81 in a row), so keep your best team alive and revive it first. (from video, Aslan, 5:00)

Set your line-ups and study the map during preparation.

Defeat defenders for Annihilation Points. When a stronghold's defenders are all beaten, it pays out by each Organization's rank there.

modes.tip: Only revive with Diamonds when your Organization calls a push.

Common mistake: spreading members over many strongholds, so none settles in time. (worked out from the rules — not tested)
Revive with Diamonds only when your Organization calls a push.
modes.unlock: Opens with the Carnival; only the top 3 Organizations from that week's Stronghold Takeover.
modes.why: A second Saturday war for the top 3. It pays Potential Lucky Coins and Limit Crystals.

modes.name: World Boss
steps: Attack daily: you get 3 attempts a day, and every challenge pays a reward.
Aim for damage milestones; single-battle and accumulated damage both pay.
Remember the boss can't be killed; it leaves after a while and the top 100 get ranking rewards.
modes.tip: Quitting halfway doesn't use an attempt.

modes.name: Twin Campaign
steps: Team up with a partner; each of you deploys one squad.
Win both battles to clear a floor (if your progress matches, either player can run both).
Wait for the floor's chests to unlock in sequence.
Clear a floor fully (boss + all chests) for a permanent stat buff.
modes.tip: Pair with an Organization mate at the same floor.

modes.name: Encounter
steps: Form a 3-player team (locked until Monday 05:00).
Fight 3 times with 3 different lineups; a unit used in one lineup can't join another that round.
Win for chests and points; your lineups can be attacked by other teams and lose you points.
modes.team: Teams 1, 2 and 3 exactly as in the guild-war table.
modes.tip: This is why building 3 teams early pays off.

modes.name: Strong Enemy Assault
steps: Check each stage's required characters and level them first.
Pick the stage order you like.
Meet the 3 star conditions in one attempt; your best single attempt counts.
Fail freely: a loss costs only 1 energy.

modes.name: Stronghold Takeover (Guild War)

org_plan.intro: Org policy from our guild leader, not a game rule. Unlike the general tip on this page to garrison what you take, members leave defense to the guild leader. In the game's words: the towers and buildings are Strongholds, every attack spends a Stronghold Command (the "attack charges" on this page) and extra ones can be bought, and defense is your Defense Team in a Stronghold's Garrison.
items: Teams: 1 strong team, 2 weak teams that only take empty tiles, and 1 strong team to hit players or Strongholds. The game allows only 3 teams per player, so one of these four jobs is dropped: ask the guild leader which one your strong team covers.
Roles: members pave the way toward the Strongholds. The guild leader mostly attacks the Strongholds to take them down, so members can save their teams.

Defense: unless you are a top-ranked player, do NOT put your Defense Team in a Stronghold's Garrison. Leave it open. The guild leader garrisons his own Defense Team to protect Strongholds from other players, because top players from strong orgs (for example Asura) can otherwise wipe out our teams.
Movement: push straight toward the Strongholds; don't spread out. Spread-out tiles invite attacks and lost Strongholds, and that loses the war. Play smart and use your attacks wisely.

Diamonds: spend at least 500 and at most 1,000 Diamonds per player per war on extra Stronghold Commands. Without that we will likely lose, and it gets too expensive for the guild leader and the few players keeping up. At the game's prices that buys 8 to 11 extra Commands (8 cost 590 Diamonds in total, 11 cost 990).
org_plan.title: Our org's Guild War plan (from the guild leader)

modes.region: game text of September 22, 2026; confirm on your server

items: Monday to Friday: every member runs the Weekly Challenge. The Organization ranking settles Monday 00:00–05:00 (points scored then don't count); only the top 8 at Saturday 10:00 enter.
Saturday 10:00–12:00, preparation: set your 3 line-ups and study the map. Lock your teams now: a team with a defeated character can't be edited later.
12:00–12:40, opening: everyone sends one team down a road toward an assigned target, and takes the tier-1 strongholds next to the Base. (research notes; not tested)
12:40–14:20, middle: retake strongholds the enemy has filled with points, rotate tired defenders, keep spending charges. (research notes; not tested)

14:20–15:00, finish: spend the charges you saved on the strongholds with the most stored points, and capture your last targets by about 14:40 so they are protected or garrisoned at the end. (research notes; not tested)
15:00: rank rewards. The top 3 go on to Stronghold Annihilation at 15:30.
sections.title: Phases and timeline

items: Hex tiles. You start at your Base and can attack only tiles next to ones you hold. A road tile can be attacked again after 30 s, a stronghold after 300 s.

Strongholds come in tiers: tier 1 near the bases, tier 2 between them, tier 3 in the middle. Higher tiers pay more points. In one war a creator narrated swings of 75–150 points at a tier 1, 600 for taking a tier 2 and 1,250 for retaking the tier 3. (creator report)

Police Station: taking it flips every tile in its area to you. Hospital: a win in its area restores 25% of the HP lost in that fight. Barracks: your characters that die in its area hit a random enemy for 1% of their max HP. Fortress: lets you garrison more teams.

"Garrisoned Troops (x/y)" shows a stronghold's defenders and its cap. The game setting allows up to 150, but the cap differs by stronghold (the war frame below shows 2/10), and a Fortress raises it. A tile you just captured is under Protection for a while, and some tiles can be destroyed so no one can hold them.
Some strongholds are held by NPC (bot) teams instead of players.
sections.title: The map

items: Attack: your strongest team, built for burst. Healing can't raise a unit above the HP it started the fight with, so heal-heavy teams lose value here.
Against NPC strongholds: skill burst and shield removal (Miza, Roma [Mad Clown], Naki [1.5th Anniversary]). The bots switch off passives for 1–2 turns, so passive-only carries struggle.
Defense: tanky units, death saves and counters. Lost HP stays lost, so the team that survives longest wins the trade.

Kiyoko's +40% basic stats and first death save work in Stronghold Takeover only, and her passive also works from back-up. If your Stronghold line-up has a back-up slot (check in game), she belongs there.

Teams are 5 characters. The guide's plan is 1 strong team plus 2 small tile teams (guild tip). The October 19 article and some creators instead want 3 full teams, with 2 on defense or as walls of weak teams; follow your Organization's call.

Team size: the game text says a team needs 5 characters to deploy (GVG_UI107), while guild players use 1–2 character tile teams (guild tip). If the game refuses a small team, make your tile teams from your 5 weakest units. (unconfirmed)
sections.title: Attack teams and defense teams

items: First: the tier 1s next to your Base and any Police Station on your route. They are cheap, start earning points early and give a first-capture reward.
Next: the 2 nearest tier 2s. Put defenders on them right away.
Don't open on the tier 3. Let rivals spend their teams on it, then take it late; that is how the winner played in the war Aslan narrated. (creator report)
Retake a stronghold after the enemy has held it a while: the steal is half of what is stored there. A stronghold held only 10 minutes is not worth much yet. (research notes; not tested)
Hit the stronghold with the fewest garrisoned teams first, and stop feeding a stronghold that has 50 or more defenders. (research notes; not tested)

Scale on an older server: player defense teams of 1.37M–1.57M CP and attack teams around 1.57M CP (frames on this page, The Spectre, January 2026). Compare your CP with the defenders' CP shown on a stronghold before you attack. (from video)
sections.title: Choosing targets

items: HP lost in a fight stays lost. It comes back slowly, only outside battle, after a 60 s wait.
Withdraw a defender that drops below about half HP and put a fresh team in, so the tired one heals. (research notes; not tested)
Revives are per character: 100 Diamonds for the first 5, then 150 for the next 10, 200 for the next 10, then 300. A whole 5-unit team costs 500 the first time. There is a cap of 300 revives.
Quick Recovery Potions cost the same counts and are the better choice for your main team. Potion and Diamond revives also pay Revival Points; the Revival Point Shop sells Panacean Star-Up Crystals.
Each of the first 9 extra charges costs 100 Diamonds or less, less than most revives, so buy charges first.
sections.title: HP and revives

items: Monday: an officer posts the Weekly Challenge boss attribute. By Wednesday everyone posts their best run. Thursday: officers check the top-20 board, and low scorers retry on Friday if you are near 8th. (research notes)
Saturday: mark up to 8 targets on the map and give each tier 2 a squad of about 5 with a leader in the Stronghold chat.
Stagger attackers on one stronghold so a fresh team hits about every 100 s; each team must wait 300 s between stronghold attacks. (research notes; not tested)
High-CP members hit strongholds; low-CP members take tier 1s and free tiles all war long and hold the walls.
Allied sister Organizations can block each other's rivals and split the map. (creator report)
sections.title: Organization coordination

items: Final rank, for every member: rank 1 pays a Lv.6 Random Potential, 10 Carnival Summon Tickets and 50,000 Talent Certificates; ranks 2–3 pay a Lv.5 Potential, 8 tickets and 30,000 or 20,000; ranks 4–10 a Lv.5 Potential and 5 tickets. (game data; per member is our reading)
Holding a stronghold until its progress bar fills pays every member 1,000, 2,000 or 3,000 Diamonds plus Cell Promoter and Eukaryote.
First captures pay an Event Summon Ticket (level 1), a Carnival Summon Ticket (level 2) or 800 Talent Certificates (level 3).
Personal Attack, Defense and Activity ranks pay Exclusive Treasure Box keys to the top players.

steps: Saturday: preparation from 10:00, battle 12:00–15:00, rank rewards at 15:00 (server time).
Each player sets 3 teams. You start from your Base, which can't be attacked, and can only attack tiles next to ones you hold.
You start with 10 attack charges and get 1 more every 20 minutes. You can buy 19 more for 2,790 Diamonds in total; the first 3 cost 50 each.
Every stronghold you hold earns points every 5 minutes. Strongholds still yours at the end pay a final share.
Taking another Organization's stronghold steals 50% of the points stored there.
Lost HP stays lost between fights and comes back slowly outside battle. Fallen characters recover slowly, or you revive them with Diamonds or Quick Recovery Potions (each revive costs more).
Healing can't raise a unit above the HP it had when the fight started.
modes.teams_needed: 3 teams per player; the game asks for 5 characters to deploy a team. The guide's plan: 1 strong team that attacks and defends, plus 2 cheap teams that only grab free tiles (guild tip).
tips: Common mistake: three medium teams that all attack. That wastes charges (guild tip).
Common mistake: a strong team spent on a free tile, which any team could take (guild tip).
Common mistake: taking a stronghold you can't garrison. When they take it back, they steal half its points.
Common mistake: sitting at 10 charges, or paying for revives before buying the cheap charges.
Common mistake: leaving the Weekly Challenge until Saturday morning; the entry check is at 10:00.
Practice in Takeover Simulation (Organization menu) before Saturday. (creator tip)

Sundays: the Global Stronghold War is cross-server and entry is by total member CP. Its steal setting is 0, but its rule text says captured points are plundered, so check in game. Either way, holding tiles pays every battle.

steps: Carnival Recruitment: the featured unit drops at 1% per pull, and every 100 pulls opens a chest whose contents change by season. Season 1 (Set Sail, likely this server's Carnival 1): 30% the featured unit, 30% a Selection Chest that offers only Kaneki [Christmas], Hinami [Christmas] or a Lv.6 Potential, 24% a Panacean Star-Up Crystal, 16% a Refinement Crystal. Season 2's chest has no Selection Chest (24% featured). Read the chest odds on each Carnival's banner, and pull only in blocks of 100.
Carnival Arena: 3 teams, best of 3, 10 tries a day (its own guide below).
Region Breakthrough: stage-by-stage fights with a locked team (its own guide below).
Carnival Exchange: spend Carnival Tokens. Tokens are not cleared when a Carnival ends.
Paragon Teams: Carnival Tokens raise a team's Paragon Level, a level boost in Carnival modes (its own guide below).
Stronghold Takeover and Stronghold Annihilation: the Saturday Organization wars (their own guides below).
Weekly Carnival quests pay about 2,000 Tokens and 1,050 Diamonds.
modes.teams_needed: Carnival Arena and Stronghold Takeover each take 3 teams, so have 3 ready before Carnival starts.
tips: Exchange order: the season unit's Ability Sphere only if you own that unit, then Potential boxes, then Limit Crystals, then Cell Promoter and Eukaryote.

steps: A Paragon Team holds several teams. Only max-level characters can join.
Carnival Tokens raise each team's Paragon Level; its members fight as if leveled above the level cap.
Max Paragon Level unlocks a Team Passive. Reroll it with Carnival Tokens for a better one.
The buff works only in Carnival modes, and all Paragon records reset when the Carnival ends.
tips: Put Tokens into one Paragon Team first: the one you use most in Carnival Arena. (research notes)
Creators reroll the first team for the hit-back effect (Retaliate). (creator tip)
